idea: A production-ready Telegram bot in Python that asynchronously downloads videos from Instagram Reels/Posts, YouTube Shorts/Videos, and Reddit videos upon user URL input, then publishes them to a specified Telegram channel with proper validation, retry, file cleanup, and error handling.
preferred_stack: Python 3.12+, aiogram 3.x, yt-dlp, aiohttp, asyncio, python-dotenv, ffmpeg, Docker + docker-compose
constraints: Use asynchronous code with asyncio and aiohttp
Store secrets only in .env or environment variables (no hardcoding)
Implement retry logic on download failures
Use tempfile for temporary storage and ensure cleanup on success and errors
Log all key events and errors using logging module
Support concurrent processing of multiple links
Provide graceful error handling and user feedback in bot
Use pydantic-settings or dotenv for configuration loading
goals: Design project folder structure as specified with clean separation of concerns
Implement configuration loading with pydantic-settings respecting .env and environment variables
Implement BaseDownloader abstraction and concrete InstagramDownloader, YouTubeDownloader, RedditDownloader using yt-dlp asynchronously with retry and timeout
Implement Telegram bot using aiogram 3.x with commands /start, /help, /status and URL input handling validating URLs then processing concurrently
Use tempfile module to store downloads in temp/, ensure cleanup on success or exception with safeguards
Constrain video size based on config MAX_VIDEO_SIZE_MB before publishing
Publish downloaded videos to specified Telegram channel asynchronously
Log all major actions and errors with Python logging configured for structured logs and logs volume
Containerize app with Docker and docker-compose including ffmpeg and volume for logs
Include README with setup, usage, configuration, docker instructions, troubleshooting
Implement graceful shutdown and healthcheck endpoint
Add typing, data models with pydantic, lint recommendations, and .gitignore
non_goals: Supporting TikTok/Twitter downloading (planned for future, not included now)
Implementing complex pipeline frameworks or external databases
Embedding keys or secrets directly in codebase
Storing videos persistently beyond temporary lifetime
Creating GUI or web interface besides the Telegram bot
Using agents, event buses, vector DBs, or RAG methods
Overengineering or adding features beyond video download, post, and cleanup pipeline
